Priya Nair
Frontend Engineer

Experience:
- Frontend Engineer at Lantern Interactive (2022-2025)
  Built accessible react interfaces in typescript for a logistics dashboard used daily by dispatchers.
  Introduced a shared component library that removed duplicated markup across four product surfaces.
  Reduced first contentful paint by deferring non critical bundles and trimming vendor javascript.
- Junior Developer at Harbor Studio (2021-2022)
  Converted static designs into responsive layouts and wrote vitest coverage for shared hooks.

Education:
- B.A. Interaction Design, Coastal College (2021)

Skills: react typescript javascript vitest tailwind accessibility responsive design storybook

# Weather Dashboard
A forecasting dashboard for planning outdoor logistics.

## Overview
A react and typescript single page application that renders current conditions and a five day forecast.
Data is fetched once per minute and cached in memory so panels never flicker between refreshes.

## Interface
The layout is responsive from narrow phones up to wide desktop displays.
Every interactive control is reachable by keyboard and announced correctly by screen readers.
Colour choices were checked against contrast guidance before they were merged.

## Testing
Component behaviour is covered with vitest and testing library assertions on rendered output.
Snapshot tests were deliberately avoided because they obscured real regressions in earlier work.

## Performance
Bundles are split per route so the initial download stays small on slow connections.
Images are served in modern formats with explicit dimensions to avoid layout shift.

# Component Library
Shared react building blocks for internal products.

## Overview
A typescript component library documented in storybook and published to a private registry.
Each component ships with prop types, usage notes, and an accessibility checklist.

## Design Tokens
Spacing, colour and typography are expressed as tokens rather than hard coded values.
Consumers theme the library by overriding tokens instead of forking components.

## Contributing
New components require a storybook story, vitest coverage, and a keyboard interaction note.
Pull requests are reviewed against the same accessibility checklist the library documents.
